#6108. Trump’s ‘invasion’ asylum ban to face justices

The border wall is seen in 2021 stretching along the U.S.-Mexico border near Columbus, N.M. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call)

The Supreme Court agreed on Friday to hear a challenge to President Donald Trump’s claims that an “invasion” at the southern border can be used to deny asylum claims by refugees.

The Trump administration had asked the justices to review a decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit that held the president could not broadly deny asylum claims under federal law. The case is the latest high-profile fight over one of Trump’s signature domestic policies.

The administration argues in its petition for the justices to take the case that the president has broad authority over asylum claims, which includes shutting down the system entirely because he has decided he will not grant any.

“The proclamation thus lawfully suspends access to asylum, which is a purely discretionary benefit. The court of appeals’ insistence that aliens are entitled to file futile asylum applications elevates empty procedures over substance,” the petition says.

Trump issued the order on his first day in office, declaring an “invasion” on the southern border and using that as a reason to deny asylum claims by refugees who present themselves there. The order is still in place, preventing asylum claims at the U.S.-Mexico border while the lawsuit plays out.

In court filings asking the justices to take the case, the administration pointed to “dramatic” reductions in illegal border crossings, which freed up resources to combat human trafficking and other threats.

In Friday’s order, the justices agreed to hear arguments over the legality of Trump’s executive order as well as whether the lower-court judge could grant an order in favor of all asylum seekers rather than just the ones who brought the suit.

Immigration rights groups initially challenged the order and won a successful ruling from a federal judge in Washington. The administration later appealed to the D.C. Circuit, where it lost at a three-judge panel before it brought the case before the justices.

The D.C. Circuit held that although federal law provides a president discretion in denying asylum claims, he cannot do so categorically.

The ACLU and immigrant rights groups who brought the case defended the ruling in their own filing. The filing argues that Congress mandated the creation of the asylum system and the president “may not invent by fiat a new removal system that eviscerates the protections Congress mandated by statute.”

Last term the justices ruled in favor of a separate policy dating to the first Trump administration that allowed officials to prevent asylum claims by stopping refugees from actually reaching the U.S. border.

A ruling in favor of the refugees could allow the administration to restart that policy and still deny asylum claims.

The case granted Friday is the latest high-profile immigration policy clash on the justices’ docket this term. Earlier this year the justices agreed to hear a challenge to the administration’s policy that most immigrants facing deportation should be detained without bond.

The justices will likely hear oral arguments and decide the case granted Friday before the end of the court’s term next June.

The case is Mullin v. Refugee and Immigrant Center for Education and Legal Services.

#6107. Chinese Passenger Claims Racism After American Airlines Tells Her To Give Up First Class Or Be Removed By Police

An American Airlines passenger says she bought first class, settled into her seat, then was threatened with police if she would not move to economy because another seat was broken. She suspects discrimination. I am not convinced race explains this, but I certainly understand wanting answers before surrendering a seat you paid for.

In an Instagram post, Cindy says she was traveling from New York JFK to Chicago with her cat when American selected her for an involuntary downgrade. Her own seat apparently worked. Another first class seat did not, leaving the airline with more passengers than usable seats.

She says employees attributed her selection to the airline’s system, threatened police involvement, and warned that refusing to move could result in the flight being canceled. She reports being offered $300 in travel credit.

“Right now we need you to move or get off the airplane.”

Broken seats happen, and someone may have to move. Having a functioning seat yourself does not necessarily protect you from being selected under an airline’s downgrade procedures.

But American should explain why you were selected and what happens to the money you paid…those are perfectly reasonable questions. American’s conditions of carriage promise an automatic refund of the fare difference when a passenger accepts transportation in a lower cabin. A future travel credit should be additional compensation, not a substitute for that refund, which is often calculated based on walk-up pricing and therefore no refund at all.

I would want written confirmation of the downgrade too. Being told to contact customer service later offers little reassurance when the immediate demand is to surrender your seat. Frankly, it’s horrible customer service.

Importantly, it isn’t clear if American Airlines sought volunteers before demanding that two passengers be downgraded. That has to be the case…it is 100% unacceptable for an involuntary downgrade if voluntary downgrades (in exchange for very generous compensation) have not been solicited.

Cindy identifies herself as Chinese and says an Indian man was the only other passenger singled out. She questions whether race, age, or gender influenced the decision (or perhaps because she wast raveling with her cat). I understand her frustration, but we need more information before calling this racism: we do not know the passengers’ relative priority or how American applied its procedures.

Still, whether racist or not, the whole matter certainly seemed uncourteous. An explanation and clear refund instructions might have prevented this confrontation…

I don’t think I’d ever insist on being dragged off a flight before giving up my seat, but AA must do a better job of making it worth someone’s while to downgrade. A passenger asking about money the airline owes her or seeking to understand the nature of the downgrade should receive an answer before a threat of police.

ETA: I wrote this last night, but see VFTW wrote about this too and identified the flight as American Airlines flight 3162 on Friday, November 27 from JFK-ORD.

#6105. American Airlines Flight Attendant Devises Impossible-To-Miss Snack Menu For Passengers Who Keep Asking What Is Available

An American Airlines flight attendant has found a clever way to show passengers their snack choices: a lighted sign on the service cart, complete with pictures, numbers, and hand signals. I like it, though I suspect someone will still ask what is available.

A video shared by Joseph M. Fares shows a snack cart topped with a sign reading “Please Choose One” in English and Spanish.

Below are pictures of three snacks, each assigned a number:

(recall, AA has recently improved its snack selection)

Illustrations of hands holding up one, two, or three fingers allow passengers to indicate their selection without saying anything. A clip-on light illuminates the menu, making it easier to read in a darkened cabin.

The text over the video offers a somewhat less charitable description:

Ha! I can appreciate the humor and agree this is such a “senior Mama” move, but I think this is a practical idea.

Cabins are noisy and passengers wear headphones, watch movies, sleep, or simply miss what the flight attendant said to the person in the row ahead. By the time the cart reaches them, they have no idea what is being offered.

Multiply that by an entire economy cabin and I can understand why a flight attendant would want a menu she can point to.

The pictures are especially useful. A passenger may not recognize a brand name or understand a spoken description, but seeing the package can make the choice much easier. The numbered options could also help someone who has difficulty hearing or does not speak English or Spanish.

Of course, the sign asks passengers to choose one. I suspect that even with the instruction prominently displayed, someone will ask for all three. And someone else will study the entire menu before asking whether there are pretzels…I have to chuckle about that because I frequently here passengers ask FAs what drinks are available when the menus are always on a menu in their seatback or on the screen.

I give this flight attendant credit. A lighted menu with pictures and numbered choices strikes me as a sensible way to make snack service easier for passengers and crew alike even though it is a very American way do doing it (and of course I mean that both in terms of the airline and the people).

There is plenty to complain about when flying, but this is something to applaud or at worst, laugh at.

#6104. Conservative firebrand Lauren Boebert ousted in Colorado

Rep. Lauren Boebert, R-Colo., leaves the Capitol after a vote on Wednesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call)

Colorado Rep. Lauren Boebert, an outspoken conservative and Second Amendment provocateur, lost her bid for a fourth term to Democrat Eileen Laubacher, a retired rear admiral in the Navy.

Laubacher was leading 48.8 percent to 47.9 percent, a margin of 3,441 votes, when The Associated Press called the race on Friday.

The red-hued 4th District, which spreads across eastern Colorado, was unexpectedly competitive this year, a sign of how deep into red turf Democrats were able to compete this year. Boebert had Donald Trump’s endorsement, but her relationship with the president has been strained at times after she began pressing for the release of files related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Laubacher proved to be a strong fundraiser, hauling in $13.7 million as of mid-October to Boebert’s $1.2 million.

Boebert has been one of the most visible and controversial members of the House GOP conference since she won an upset primary in the 3rd District over five-term incumbent Republican Scott Tipton in 2020.

A newcomer to electoral politics, she quickly positioned herself as a disruptor on Capitol Hill, heckling former President Joe Biden during his 2022 State of the Union address and tangling with a fellow GOP firebrand, former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene of Georgia, on the House floor.

In 2023, Boebert was embroiled in an embarrassing incident in a Denver theater that was captured on surveillance video. She subsequently embarked on an apology tour.

Running for reelection the first time in the 3rd District, which is centered around Colorado’s rural Western Slope, Boebert barely won a closer-than-expected race against Democrat Adam Frisch in 2022. When Frisch announced he was trying again in 2024, Boebert switched to the 4th District, which had been considered far friendlier terrain for the GOP.

This year, Democrats won all of Colorado’s House seats, except in the 3rd District, which is held by Rep. Jeff Hurd.

Mary Ellen McIntire contributed to this report.

#6102. United Airlines Adds Three Special Flights To Spare Marching Band A Bus Ride From New York To Texas

A Texas high school marching band faced a long bus ride home after bad weather postponed the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade and disrupted its travel plans. Then United Airlines stepped in, arranging three additional flights to Houston for nearly 450 people. This is an airline story worth celebrating.

The Pride of Pearland Band and Color Guard had traveled to New York for its first appearance in the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. But when severe weather pushed the parade from Thursday to Saturday, the group faced a rather expensive dilemma: its trip was supposed to end Friday.

As the AP reports, supporters quickly raised $350,000 to help cover the extended stay. That helped keep the band in New York, but getting everyone home remained a problem.

The group could not find enough airline seats until Monday and Tuesday. The alternative was chartering buses back to Texas after the parade.

A United spokesperson explained that a customer service leader learned about the situation on Thanksgiving morning and began working with colleagues to find another solution. The result was three additional flights to Houston: two from Newark and one from New York LaGuardia.

“These were additional flights that had not been previously planned, so they needed free aircraft and crews.”

That meant finding available airplanes and coordinating crews to operate them during a very busy holiday travel period.

I struggle enough rearranging travel for my family of four. Doing it for nearly 450 people over Thanksgiving weekend sounds like a nightmare.

Of course, buses would have gotten everyone home eventually. But after extending the trip and performing in the parade, a long road journey from New York to Texas would have been an exhausting saga.

I appreciate that someone at United heard about the problem and started making calls. It would have been easy to sympathize, point to the available flights several days later, and leave the school to figure it out. Instead, employees found a way to add flights. That deserves credit, as do the donors who made it possible for the band to stay and perform.

United arranged three extra Houston flights so the Pearland group could avoid a grueling bus ride home after the postponed parade. We spend plenty of time discussing what airlines get wrong. Here, employees worked together to make a difficult situation much easier for hundreds of travelers. Well done, United.

#6098. China Southern Orders 50 737 MAX Jets

A subsidiary of China Southern Airlines has agreed to buy 50 Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft, Reuters reported Tuesday.

The airplanes, which have a total list price of $7.4 billion, will be used by Xiamen Airlines, which is based in Fujian. Deliveries are expected from 2031 to 2034.

The deal is Boeing’s largest with a Chinese operator in nearly a decade. The country largely shifted toward Airbus aircraft as relations with the U.S. frayed.

President Donald Trump hoped to reverse that trend during his state visit to China in May. Trump discussed a potential purchase directly with Chinese President Xi Jinping, and even brought along Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg for the summit. Ultimately, Beijing agreed to buy 200 aircraft from Boeing, fewer than analysts expected, but still notable considering Boeing’s drought in the country.

Trump said earlier this week that he thinks China will buy 250 more aircraft from Boeing. He did not provide details or say where that information came from.

China Southern said the new aircraft will help Xiamen expand after it relocates to the new Xiamen Xiang’an International Airport. The facility will replace Xiamen Gaoqi International Airport as Xiamen’s main gateway.

#6096. Former Washington Rep. Jim McDermott dies at 89

Former Rep. Jim McDermott, D-Wash., is seen in a vineyard near his cottage in Civrac-en-Médoc, France, on March 20, 2024. (Ariel Cohen/CQ Roll Call)

Former Rep. Jim McDermott, D-Wash., a fierce advocate for universal health care and outspoken war critic who served 28 years in Congress, died Thursday at the age of 89, his family announced.

In a roughly 50-year career in state and federal office, the salty-tongued, liberal lawmaker from Seattle won both praise and criticism for pushing an aggressive agenda focused on expanding health care to all Americans.

As the top Democrat on the House Ways and Means Health Subcommittee, McDermott defended the 2010 Affordable Care Act that expanded health insurance to millions of Americans, while critics complained it did little to control costs.

“Jim was one of the first and most powerful voices fighting to fix our broken health care system in Congress,” Sen. Patty Murray, D-Wash., wrote on X. “He was passionate and fearless — and left a tremendous legacy on WA state and its people. My thoughts are with Congressman McDermott’s family and loved ones during this difficult time.”

When McDermott announced his retirement from Congress in 2016, then-President Barack Obama praised him in a statement as “a much-needed voice for his most vulnerable constituents.”

Born and raised in Illinois, McDermott came from a poor, conservative and deeply religious family. His father, a bond underwriter, and his mother, a telephone operator and homemaker, started a church in the garage of their two-bedroom home. His three siblings slept in one bedroom; his parents in the other. McDermott, the oldest child, had the couch.

He attended the conservative evangelical Wheaton College. His bend toward liberalism began during medical school at the University of Illinois, when he voted for John F. Kennedy in the 1960 presidential election. After a stint in the U.S. Navy Medical Corps from 1968-1970, McDermott won his first seat in the Washington state House in 1970 running on an anti-war platform.

He continued his anti-war stances in Congress, voting against the 2002 resolution authorizing the use of military force in Iraq. In 2013, he opposed U.S. intervention in Syria and was one of only 20 House members to vote against new sanctions on Iran.

Shortly after he retired from Congress, McDermott settled on a new life for himself by moving to a small town in southwestern France, where he admired some of the public policies he had fought hard to deliver in Washington with mixed success.

“I spent 16 years in the Washington state legislature trying to get single-payer health care,” he recalled in a 2024 interview with CQ Roll Call at his home about 90 minutes outside of Bourdeaux. “Then I spent nearly 30 years in Congress trying to get single-payer. Then I came to France and in three months I had single-payer. Was that mind-blowing? You bet.”

As he said, McDermott dedicated much time in the Washington state legislature to trying to create a single-payer system. When that didn’t work out, he developed the Washington State Basic Health Program, a health coverage system for the unemployed and working poor — the first state program of its kind.

Then, once he got to Washington, he tried to work with then-First Lady Hillary Clinton to hatch a federal single-payer program, but that effort came to naught. He later backed the Affordable Care Act and tried to pass his own legislation in 2015 for comprehensive health care coverage.

“The only way to truly ensure that access to quality health care is a right enjoyed by every American is through a single-payer system,” he said in a statement at the time.

McDermott will also be remembered for some of the attacks he leveled against Republicans. In the most notorious incident, he was ordered to pay then-Rep. John A. Boehner of Ohio — who later became speaker — nearly $1.1 million in 2008 after releasing a recording of a 1996 cell phone call between Boehner and then-Speaker Newt Gingrich. McDermott maintained it was worth the fight, and the cost of the settlement, to protect free speech.

“Jim McDermott was as big as it gets in Washington state politics,” Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash., wrote on Facebook. “Smart, funny, and Irish, Jim McDermott will be missed.”

#6094. 12 Standout 2026 Black Friday Cruise Deals to Take You Around the World for Less

Deals and pricing updated as of 5:03 p.m. on November 27, 2026.

It's go time, cruisers. We've officially reached one of the best times of the year to book a cruise—Cyber Week. Despite falling just before wave season, cruise lines of all shapes and sizes are slashing prices on sailings this week, with some extending the travel-by window well into 2028. This means that whether you're considering something last-minute (perhaps spontaneous NYE plans?) or have a sailing in mind for 2027 or 2028, now may very well be the ideal time to book and save serious dollars on trips around the world.

Below, I've spotlighted Cyber Week deals from 12 cruise lines Traveler readers know and love. There's a variety of options—river cruises, ocean voyages, and expedition ships are all in on the fun—with itineraries taking guests everywhere from the Galápagos and the Nile to the Arctic and Antarctic regions. Read on for the best Black Friday cruise deals to book right now.

Quark Expeditions' Ultramarine sailing in the Arctic

If you've ever dreamed of hopping on a polar cruise and exploring the Arctic or Antarctic, now's your chance to do so without stretching your budget quite so far. Quark Expeditions is offering up to 40% off select polar sailings when booked by December 3. Limited cabins are available, and once they’re gone, they’re gone, so if you're eager, be sure to book before your dream trip fills up.

There are many enticing itineraries to choose from—Svalbard in Spring, Essential Patagonia, South Greenland: Alpine Exploration by Helicopter—all of which are particularly well-suited to travelers seeking out enrichment and immersion opportunities or the chance to come eye-to-eye with majestic wildlife. For those set on crossing the Great White Continent (Antarctica) off their bucket list but are wary of the Drake Passage, the Antarctic Express allows you to bypass that sometimes treacherous passage and fly in.

A contemporary premium line well-versed in sophisticated design, elevated dining, and high-quality service, Celebrity Cruises is regularly selected as one of our readers' favorite cruise lines. On Black Friday, take 75% off second guest fares and save up to $1,200 per room (both discounts are an increase from last year's sale!). With more than 600 sailings to choose from across all seven continents, you'll have no trouble finding a destination that suits the whole group.

Virgin Voyages carved out its own lane when it first set sail in 2021, and the cheeky adults-only line has maintained a loyal cohort in the years since. This year's Cyber Week deals are strong enough to have even recent sailors planning their next getaway, and might just bring along some fresh navigators too. Book by December 3 to score up to 80% off your second guest and up to $800 in free drinks (depending on your cabin category). Itineraries include transatlantic and repositioning cruises as well as sailings in North America, the Caribbean, and Europe. And with travel dates as far out as October 28, 2028, you're in no rush to put it on the calendar.

The resort-like pool deck on board Oceania Vista

With more than 600 ports of call, Oceania Cruises can take you nearly anywhere you want to go. During the culinary-focused cruise line's Black Friday sale, which runs through December 1, travelers can save up to 50% on all 2027 voyages. The geographic options are endless: Sail from Bali to Hong Kong, Barcelona to Rome, Singapore to Cape Town, Montreal to Miami, and more.

Seabourn's Black Friday sale is a good one: Book a cruise and get an autimatic upgrade to a Veranda Suite, 15% off your deposit, and $2,000 in onboard ship credit, which can be put toward spa services, curated shore excursions, and exclusive Reserve wine list bottles and optional wine pairings. As for the fine print: Full world and grand sailings are excluded, and you'll need to book by December 8, 2026.

A luxury experience awaits onboard Regent—and through December 1, it can come at a significantly lowered cost. Cruises are up to 40% off, with up to $500 in shipboard credit offered per suite, plus more savings for past guests. There are more than 90 sailings to choose from, with options in Europe, the Caribbean, Asia, and Australia. Birdwatchers, you'll want to check out the 7-Night Birdwatchers Haven Cruise through Alaska.

Royal Caribbean's newest ship, Legend of the Seas

No need to rush here—through December 7, take up to $1,000 off select cruise fares, enjoy free cruise fares for third and fourth guests sharing a stateroom, and snag up to $250 in onboard credits. Beyond that, you'll get up to 50% off onboard extras, including beverage packages, internet access, and shore excursions. These deals span tons of itineraries visiting the Caribbean, Europe, and Alaska, including ones on Royal Caribbean's newest ships like the Legend of the Seas, which just made its US debut from Fort Lauderdale, Florida, on November 8. Already itching for warmer weather? There are last-minute January and February cruises available starting at $199 per person!

Well-suited to couples looking for a laid-back but still buzzy cruise atmosphere, Holland America Line calls in ports around the world. During its Black Friday sale, travelers can get up to 30% off cruise fares, as well as perks like free prepaid stateroom tips, so long as they book by Sunday, November 29. These are some steep savings—sail to the Bahamas and Dominican Republic on a seven-day cruise for just $399 per person, or head to the Western Caribbean and Mexico for the same amount of time and pay just $449 per person.

MSC Cruises' Black Friday sale is officially live! Through Friday, November 27, take up to 40% off cruises and score up to $1,000 in onboard credit. Other perks include free balcony upgrades and kids sail free opportunities. This is a line with a little something for everyone—it's family-friendly, but the MSC Yacht Club ship-within-a-ship experience is ideal for those looking for a more peaceful ambiance. While it's particularly popular when it comes to Mediterranean cruises, its ships also sail to the Caribbean, Alaska, and Northern Europe.

Princess is a premium cruise line known for its Alaska sailings, onboard hospitality, and of course, playing host to The Love Boat in the ’70s. During its Cyber Week sale, the line is offering guests up to 50% off cruise fares, up to $800 in instant savings, and free fares for third and fourth guests on select voyages (family travelers, did you hear that?). The savings—which put starting rates at just $294 per person—are applicable across a range of itineraries, whether you're looking to explore Alaska, make Euro summer plans, escape the winter cold in the Caribbean or Mexico, or venture as far as Australia and New Zealand.

If luxury river cruising with smaller crowds is more your speed, consider sailing with Uniworld; its ships cap out at just 158 guests. You've got plenty of time to take advantage of its Cyber Week sale; the Journey Together discounts mean that if you book by December 18, the second guest (in the same stateroom) can sail for 50% off on standout itineraries down the Danube, Nile, Rhine, and more. Already planning further ahead? Book a cruise by March 31, 2027, to save up to 20% on select 2028 trips.

Is Norway on your 2027 travel bucket list? Expedition line HX knows the region well, and through December 2, is offering up to 20% off scenic journeys along Norway's coast with the region's majestic fjords in your sight line. Other all-inclusive expedition sailings are up to 40% off—sail to Antarctica, Alaska, Greenland, or the Galápagos Islands with HX.

#6093. Trump administration ups ante on aviation funds after ground stop

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy leaves a House Republican Conference meeting in the Capitol on July 21. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call)

Top administration officials doubled down on calls for Congress to supply additional funds for an ongoing air traffic modernization effort after they said old equipment contributed to the need for a nationwide ground stop of flights on Friday.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin increased their ask to $50 billion on Friday night, a day after Duffy and White House budget chief Russ Vought formally requested $30.1 billion.

The increased allotment, which the administration officials didn’t fully flesh out, comes after the nation’s air traffic control system experienced “instability” in its radar and communications at certain facilities earlier in the day, Duffy told reporters.

He said “inconsistency in the data” being issued by those systems led to implementation of the nationwide ground stop, saying the order was given out of “an abundance of caution” before being lifted about four hours later.

During a Friday night White House briefing, Duffy and Mullin explained the issues were driven by “an incredibly old air traffic control system.”

Earlier in the day, the stoppage had caused mass confusion and raised questions about potential terror attacks, or artificial intelligence breakouts resulting from new software the agency is rolling out. While Mullin said “we’re not ruling out anything,” he explained that “the public was never at danger through this process.”

Still, Duffy called the incident “an emergency” while calling for additional modernization funds.

“This is an emergency,” he said. “I want $50 billion. President Trump is a builder. He’s going to build this network and deliver for the American people. But the president can’t deliver for America unless the Congress delivers the money to make it happen.”

The latest figure is $19.1 billion higher than the figure Duffy and Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought called on congressional appropriators to approve in a Thursday letter.

Mullin said the new $50 billion figure was an administration estimate for a “complete overhaul of the system” which has been going through a “patchwork” upgrade process that may have overwhelmed the older equipment still being used.

“We need someone to come in and build the whole system," Mullin said. "Nickel and diming it together does not work."

Thursday’s call for $30.1 billion echoes a White House-backed bill that Sen. Eric Schmitt, R-Mo., introduced in September, which would provide $10.1 billion for air traffic control upgrades, including $2 billion for "cloud computing and national airspace system telecommunications."

Those funds would come after $12.5 billion allocated to the effort through the July 2025 reconciliation law that Duffy and Vought called a “down-payment."

Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee Republicans touted those already-appropriated funds in a social media post. They pointed to $1.9 billion provided in the reconciliation law that would go toward upgrading air route traffic control centers, which guide planes across long distances after departure and which the FAA had cited as the cause of the problem.

The 22 air route traffic control centers across the country guide aircraft using instrument-dependent flight plans. Under such plans, pilots use instruments, electronic navigation and air traffic control assistance to guide them and maintain separation from other aircraft in certain airspaces.

The committee’s majority said Friday's outage highlighted the need to prioritize modernization of the air route traffic control centers, arguing that President Lyndon B. Johnson was in office the last time a new one was built.

Commerce ranking member Maria Cantwell, D-Wash., said in a statement Friday night that the panel is looking into FAA and airspace telecommunications issues.

“Technology issues related to how planes communicate through primary frequencies, backup frequencies, and other issues will be something the Commerce Committee will be reviewing,” Cantwell said.

Cantwell is poised to take the committee's gavel come January as Democrats assume the majority in the Senate.

In a joint statement Friday night, House Transportation and Infrastructure Chairman Sam Graves, R-Mo., and ranking member Rick Larsen, D-Wash., called the communication failures “concerning” and said their committee would “thoroughly review the issues that led to this nationwide ground stop.”

Both committees have also been in monthslong negotiations over dueling aviation safety bills responding to the January 2025 midair collision near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport that killed 67 people.

At issue in those negotiations is which location transmission technology should be mandated to aid in air traffic control operations and allow aircraft to maintain appropriate distance. Leaders have said they hope to reach a deal in the lame-duck session.

Wyndham Rewards recently revised its fixed award chart, expanding from three to four redemption tiers.

The 15,000- and 30,000-point tiers remain, while free nights now start at 5,000 points instead of 7,500. Wyndham also added a 45,000-point tier for a select number of its highest-tier hotels and redistributed thousands of properties across all four tiers.

The new top tier is 50% higher than the former 30,000-point maximum, a devaluation in anyone's book. However, the new astonishingly low 5,000-point tier was what caught my attention. What exactly do you get for so few Wyndham Rewards points?

As someone who can't resist a great deal, I checked into one of these hotels to find out whether it was an amazing new sweet spot or a night I would rather forget.

Related: Wyndham Rewards guide: How to earn and redeem points, elite status and more

On a recent visit to Kansas and Missouri, I checked the Wyndham Rewards website and saw that the area had several properties for just 5,000 points per night.

I chose the Super 8 by Wyndham Riverside/Kansas City, mainly for its proximity to the beautiful new Kansas City International Airport (MCI). The next morning, I was flying to Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) before continuing to Europe in a lie-flat seat for less than the price of a cup of coffee.

At the time of booking, the hotel had a 2.8-out-of-5 score based on 84 ratings on Wyndham's website, which did not fill me with confidence. However, the Wyndham Rewards member rate for my night was $96.21 including taxes and fees. Redeeming 5,000 points therefore gave me 1.92 cents per Wyndham point, about 3.5 times TPG's November 2026 valuation of 0.55 cents per Wyndham point.

Related: It’s easy to earn Wyndham Diamond status — here’s how and why you should care

I took a Lyft from downtown Kansas City, Missouri, to Riverside, a small suburb on the north bank of the Missouri River. First impressions of the property were that it was pretty remote, with nothing really nearby other than the Argosy Casino.

There was plenty of parking, and the 48 rooms were spread across a two-story motor-inn-style building.

While the property was less than 20 years old and was renovated in 2010, the rather garish lime-green lobby looked ready for another refresh.

I was quickly helped by a very friendly attendant, who I believe was the franchisee, and his wife, who also greeted me warmly.

There were several property rules listed on the counter with normal restrictions on smoking and pets in rooms.

What raised an eyebrow was the rule that visitors were allowed in guest rooms for only 60 minutes maximum, which made me wonder what kind of visitors might be passing through the doors and for what purpose in one-hour blocks.

The attendant thanked me for being a Wyndham Rewards member and quickly handed me my room key. So far, the experience had been better than the 2.8-out-of-5 rating suggested, but the room would be the biggest test.

I nervously opened the door to find a comfortable room with a king-size bed, plenty of pillows, a large flat-screen TV, a minifridge and a workspace.

Like the lobby, I doubt this decor will win any design awards, but it was clean, quiet and comfortable, and everything worked.

The separate bathroom had a tub/shower combo and a spotless toilet with several towels for me to choose from.

If I had one complaint about the room, it was that the showerhead was pulling away from the bathroom wall, but it still provided a steady flow of hot water.

The property was light on other amenities: There was no fitness center, swimming pool, bar or restaurant. However, the Argosy Casino was a few minutes' walk away, so there was plenty to keep me occupied for the evening.

After a good night's uninterrupted sleep, all guests even received a complimentary breakfast, with toast, cereals, juice and coffee available.

This is a great deal for a 5,000 point redemption with no resort fee.

Related: How I earned 24,500 points from $180 in hotel stays

The staff bid me a friendly farewell when I checked out, and I was on my way to the airport after a comfortable, peaceful and stress-free stay.

Wyndham Rewards are easy to earn, as they transfer at a 1:1 rate from the following transferable rewards:

But the best transfer option is for anyone with Wells Fargo Rewards points. This is because rather than transferring at a 1:1 rate, they transfer at a much more generous 1:2 rate. This means you would only need 2,500 Wells Fargo points to book a 5,000-point Wyndham Rewards hotel night, and Wells Fargo points can be transferred in any increments, unlike the strict 1,000-point increments of most transferable rewards.

Given that Wyndham Rewards properties offering 5,000-point nights regularly sell these nights for around $100 cash, this is an easy way to get around 4 cents per Wells Fargo point, more than twice TPG's valuation of Wells Fargo Rewards points.

Barclays also offers four Wyndham Rewards branded credit cards. Depending on the card and, in some cases, when it was opened, eligible cardholders receive a 10%, 20%, or 25% discount on free-night redemptions. That reduces a standard 5,000-point night to 4,500, 4,000 or 3,750 points, respectively.

Wyndham's new 5,000-point redemptions will not put you in a luxury hotel, but this stay was terrific value for money and delivered a clean, quiet room, a comfortable bed and a simple breakfast before an early flight.

The decor was dated, and the loose showerhead fixture needed attention. Even so, the friendly service and uninterrupted night's sleep were far better than the hotel's 2.8-out-of-5 rating had led me to expect. For a one-night stay near an airport, I would give it 4 out of 5.

Redeeming 5,000 Wyndham Rewards points instead of paying the nearly $100 member rate will give you 2 cents' worth per point. Even better, a traveler transferring from Wells Fargo Rewards would need just 2,500 points for the same award — I can't think of a more valuable way to use Wells Fargo points.

I would happily stay at a property like this again for just 5,000 Wyndham Rewards points per night.

With service to all four major Hawaiian Islands—Oahu, Maui, Kauai, and the Big Island—the airline makes it easy to plan a trip around everything from Waikiki’s beach scene to Maui’s coastal drives and Kauai’s lush landscapes. Its Black Friday promotion offers a chance to save up to 30% on flights to Hawaii, whether you’re hoping to get away during the winter months or plan ahead for a warmer-weather vacation in 2027.

When it comes to savvy ways to fly, it’s no secret that Skyscanner provides heaps of flight options and routes where value is front and center. If you’re looking to score cheap flights over the Black Friday weekend, you can count on the site for price drops on airfare this weekend through Travel Tuesday. Along with vacation packages, hotel deals (at up to 35% off), and an app for price tacking, the Skyscanner website has an entire guide on and around Travel Tuesday itself—from advice on reducing fees to using shared loyalty points and beyond.

Whether you are mapping out a holiday road trip or chasing winter sun, scoring the right car rental deal is half the adventure. While highly regarded car rental company Avis has not yet rolled out an official Travel Tuesday promotion ahead of the December 1 event, you won’t have to wait to lock in some stellar savings. Right now, you can trim up to 35% off base rates simply by choosing the Pay Now option online, or unlock up to 30% off with Avis’s current discount code AWD S169100.

Sometimes the best part of a getaway is having the freedom to take the scenic route. Turo, the car-sharing marketplace that lets travelers book vehicles directly from local hosts, is offering first-time US guests $50 off their first trip with promo code TURO50TT. The deal applies to reservations of $250 or more booked between now and December 8, 2026, for trips taking place November 28, 2026, through January 4, 2027. It’s a good excuse to pick out a car for a holiday road trip, a winter weekend away, or a few days exploring somewhere new at your own pace. The offer is limited to the first 4,000 redemptions, with one use per guest.

Book a discounted tour to the cloud forests of Costa Rica.

A destination is only part of a great trip; what you do once you get there can make it all the more memorable. GetYourGuide’s Black Friday sale offers a little extra incentive to fill out those plans, with discounts of up to 50% on select tours, activities, and attraction tickets worldwide. And the options are wonderfully broad, whether you’re hoping to get inside major landmarks without the usual lines, learn to make a vintage coin ring in Kyoto, take a day trip to Hallstatt from Vienna, or head out on a northern lights excursion in Tromsø.

For anyone already counting down to their first day on the mountain, Black Friday weekend is a good time to start mapping out the rest of the ski season. Luckily for shredders, Epic Pass is offering up to 65% savings on skiing and riding, with options for different budgets and schedules, from the Epic Day Pass (starting at $50 per day) to the full Epic Pass, which includes unlimited, unrestricted access to more than 90 resorts.

That means days at big-name mountains in Vail, Breckenridge, Park City, and Whistler. There’s also new young adult pricing, with skiers and riders ages 13 to 20 saving 20%. Passes go off sale December 6, and there’s another reason to book a mountain escape ASAP: Epic Pass holders can save up to 35% on winter lodging through Vail Resorts’s Lodging Cyber Sale, running until December 7.

If you’ve got a sudden urge to get up and go, this is G Adventures’s biggest sale of the year—and it includes hundreds of early Travel Tuesday deals with up to 30% off tours and experiences across the globe. With some trips departing in the next 60 days, we’re talking discounts on some of the group’s most-loved and top-rated trips, including Thailand Island Hopping on the West Coast and chasing Costa Rica: Coastlines and Clouds Forests. If your schedule’s flexible and your passport’s ready, this is the kind of spontaneous deal you jump on before it disappears.

For travelers who like to get out and explore, EF Adventures builds its small-group trips around active experiences, from hiking and cycling to kayaking and other outdoor excursions. Lucky for those adventure artists, this Black Friday sale offers up to $600 off select 2027 and 2028 itineraries, with options ranging from cycling through Tuscany or Spain’s Costa Brava to hiking the Camino de Santiago or exploring Japan’s Alps. Another plus: Trips pair these adventures with local guides, boutique accommodations, and opportunities to experience each destination beyond its most familiar sights.

#6088. Avianca Adds New U.S. Route

Colombian flag carrier Avianca is adding a new connection to the U.S. Northeast.

Starting Feb. 2, 2027, the airline will offer service between Barranquilla and New York-JFK.

Flights will operate four times weekly using Airbus A320-family aircraft, each with up to 180 seats.

“The launch of this nonstop route to New York reaffirms our commitment to [Barranquilla] and the entire Colombian Caribbean region,” Avianca President Gabriel Oliva said in a statement. “We want to continue connecting regions with major international markets, making travel easier, supporting tourism, and contributing to Colombia’s economic development.”

Avianca currently serves JFK from Bogota, Cartagena, Medellín, Pereira, Colombia, Guatemala City, San Salvador, El Salvador, Quito, and Guayaquil. From Barranquilla, it flies to Miami, Bogota, Medellín, and Cali.

#6087. Your December 2026 Horoscope: This Month Brings the Calm After the Storm

Steph Koyfman is a writer and astrologer best known for her work as Lady Cazimi. She writes the monthly horoscope for Condé Nast Traveler's Women Who Travel.

Your December 2026 horoscope has landed! This month brings us into a lull between louder, more energetic pockets of astrology, but it’s also not quite “circle back season,” either. Rather than mentally check out now and defer projects and decisions until January, this is actually the time to be wrapping things up. Mercury is now barreling full steam ahead after its direct station, and Venus is playing catch-up as it re-enters Scorpio and completes the retrograde story that began all the way back in August. As if that weren’t enough, Saturn and Neptune are stationing direct (on December 10 and 12, respectively) while Jupiter stations retrograde (also on December 12), and Mars is already slowing down to go retrograde on January 10 (okay, so that's one we can circle back on after the holidays). Functionally, December is creating a natural hinge point in the year, a bookend for us to move out of one mode and enter another. It is a fork in the road where we may be asked to put down what we’ve been doing so we can pick up what we need to do next.

In other words: Don’t expect this month to be uneventful, but do expect some relative calm compared to the insane baseline that the rest of 2026 has created for us. This is not a bad time to get away and go somewhere, though it wouldn’t be shocking if you needed to bring some work with you on the road or devote some mental real estate to an important decision that’s weighing on you. Logistically, travel could be problematic between December 6 and 9, when Mercury enters Sagittarius and immediately runs into a chaotic little traffic jam with Mars and Uranus. The New Moon in Sagittarius on December 8 launches a new six-month journey out of that dust cloud, so whatever you get into around that timeframe could set the tone for the immediate future. Maybe you’ll snap at someone, maybe you’ll mess around and find out, maybe you’ll have a misadventure that redirects you in one way or another.

Venus will be in Scorpio all month beginning December 4, so this moment in time will also be tinged with a moody glamor. This would probably be the time to avoid the most popular normie spots at your destination and opt to enjoy the things you like that other people may find offputting or unappealing. Find ways to create the intimacy you crave, maybe by skipping the crowded spots and opting for the cozier places you’ll be tempted to gatekeep later. In the context of everything Venus went through over the last couple of months, this is where we get a more complete sense of closure and an opportunity to start acting on the insights and revelations we’ve had. What would it look like to give yourself something that a former version of you craved so badly?

Astrologer's note: Below we refer to your signs as “rising” signs, also known as your ascendant sign. Horoscopes are more accurate when read this way—using your birth time and location, you can quickly find your rising sign online (it takes less than 30 seconds).

Looks like it’s time to lock in and recommit yourself to what you’re really here to do. As Saturn and Neptune both station direct together in mid-December, you, too, will feel the pressure to stop dilly dallying or being avoidant toward your own sacred mission in life. You may have had to put things on hold back in July, or maybe just enter into a more indeterminate state of being that gave you the flexibility to make adjustments. Things are solidifying now and becoming less ambiguous, but this isn’t just about getting back to business. You may also need to take radical accountability for the mess you made this past year while you were throwing spaghetti at the wall to see what sticks. There’s absolutely nothing wrong with the fact that you tried something and it didn’t work—it’s commendable! But what’s different about right now is that you have the resources to reinforce the wobbly foundations and give things another shot in a way that might produce a better result.

The thing about locking in is that you should probably expect things to be a little bit of a grind (at least at first). Your ruling planet, Mars, is already slowing down to go retrograde next month, and you will likely feel your energy and effectiveness flagging a bit as we get closer to the new year. This isn’t a reason to feel discouraged, just a heads up that moving forward will require you to seriously retool your approach this time. You will know pretty quickly what’s not going to cut it anymore, particularly when it comes to your working methods and productivity hacks. For now, try to be industrious while you have the capacity for it, and be mindful to not overdo it at your desk or at the gym.

There is reason to suspect you might be traveling this month, or otherwise devoting significant energy to your learning pursuits. However, there’s also a certain gravitational pull coming from home base as the full moon in Cancer shows you something important about where you’re currently tethered on December 23. Perhaps you’ll be scouting new locations to live as you plan a long-distance move, or maybe travel will be a form of homecoming one way or another. Be mindful of any trips you need to take between December 6 and 9, because this could be a stressful and chaotic time to fly or navigate an unfamiliar map. Give yourself the grace (and extra time) to be late, delayed, or to make a cringey mistake when you’re speaking another language. What matters is that you can always laugh about it later.

You’re making a renewed bid for connection, but this time, it’s not coming from the same starved, unfulfilled place you were in a couple months ago. Your ruling planet, Venus, reenters Scorpio on December 4, bringing the full harvest of the recent retrograde along and threading some sense of closure or forward movement into your relationships. While this might feel vulnerable (and yes, a bit edgy) for you, it’s only new territory in the sense that you’re not approaching it as the same person you were even back in October. You are changed, and it shows in the way you’re relating to others going forward, as well as in the updated set of standards you have for your romantic partnerships, business collaborations, and friendships. This inner shift might yield a concrete result within a few months’ time, like you’re leveling up and accessing new ways of being partnered in the world. For now, let December be your proving ground.

Your annual peak travel season also turns up at the end of the month, just in time for the holidays as usual. In particular, Mercury’s transit through Capricorn (your 9th house of foreign travel, learning, and spirituality) starts on December 25 and lasts through January 13, which encourages you to be on the move physically or intellectually. However, Mercury must first pass through a security check via a square to Saturn on December 30, and it will also be very combust the entire time, aka too close to the Sun for comfort. You might have to put more effort than usual into getting all the logistics to flow smoothly, to be understood by people who don’t speak your language, and to get your ideas across more generally. On the other hand, this energy is potentially useful for flying under the radar.

On December 29, Venus will square the lunar nodes, which brings you to a crossroads of some kind (particularly where relationships are concerned). There are important decisions to make about other people, who you wish to be joined to, and what that means for the direction of your life in general. It could be that you’re approaching a turning point in your vision for home and family, and it’s going to matter right now whether you’re sufficiently aligned on those things with your current partner (or any future people you choose to build with). If you’ve been on the hunt for a new home or have been wrapped up in a home improvement project, expect to either hit a pause or change tactics as Jupiter goes retrograde on December 12, but also be open to what’s emerging. You might realize you feel different about your current living situation by the time the month is up, or maybe you’ll notice that your own goalposts are shifting.

Life is setting you free to think about new problems for a change. Whatever you were stuck on over the past couple months probably took longer than you bargained for, but your project will be that much better for all the time you spent debugging the code. Mercury squares the lunar nodes on December 1, bringing you to a turning point regarding a work, pet, or health matter. You did your due diligence and even sought out a second opinion or diagnosis. Now, it’s time to make a choice and move out of decision paralysis. It’s scary because it feels more final than it did when you were merely researching your options, but it makes sense to start wrapping up this process now. Venus will spend most of December covering Mercury’s tracks in Scorpio, so you can gently start putting your care and devotion toward healing or creating cohesion in this part of your life again.

Personally, you will find the second week of the month more challenging, anyway. Mercury enters Sagittarius on December 6, your 7th house of relationships, only to immediately run into a messy confrontation with Mars and Uranus on the 8th and 9th. This looks a bit dramatic and maybe needlessly provocative, but it does seem as though some blunt honesty will make the rounds and shake up the dynamics in dire need of a reality check. This is not the time to bite your tongue for the sake of maintaining superficial harmony, but things could easily go off the rails with this one, so try to choose your words intentionally and exercise a little bit of impulse control. You are potentially setting the tone for the next couple months when it comes to your relationships and social ecosystem more broadly, which could be a good thing if it lets you finally say the quiet part out loud.

The end of the month affords you a little more focused concentration to get your financial house in order. The full moon in Cancer on December 23 brings a money matter to a head and brings your true budgeting power to light, and Mercury will enter Capricorn on December 25 to redirect your attention toward longer-term financial planning. These next couple of weeks could be a good time to literally map out a timeline of your year and start allocating resources toward the trips, experiences, and big purchases you’ll need to save up for. You’ve probably gotten a good amount of mileage out of your weekender bag these last few months especially, but with Jupiter stationing retrograde in your 3rd house of short trips, you will likely have to slow your roll with that until April, or maybe just reconsider how you’re going about all that movement. Maybe it’s time to give the car a rest and take the train instead?

It looks like your efforts are finally bearing fruit, and that, of course, comes with a new set of problems for you to tackle. There’s a full moon in Cancer on December 23, which imbues the entire month with the suggestion that you’ll have exciting personal news to share very soon. Meanwhile, there are multiple clues all pointing to work things moving forward, or maybe just reaching the next step of whatever your service to society or your family looks like. In so many words, it’s time to do a little bit more of the thing that scares you, because this is precisely the thing that expands you. Mid-month, Saturn and Neptune both station direct in your 10th house of career and public reputation, concluding a somewhat more provisional chapter you’ve been in since July. Maybe things have been up in the air with work, maybe your boss left a vacancy, maybe you were focusing on other priorities during the second half of 2026. Now, there’s a sense here that “play time is over,” and it’s time to get back to the heavy lifting of your most intimidating ambitions. Yes, you may feel disoriented and like you’re leading an army without a map of your own, but you’re here for a reason. You got this.

Things appear to be brewing in your love life too, or at bare minimum, in your pursuit of happiness and personal fulfillment. Venus spends the month in Scorpio, your 5th house of romance, pleasure, and creative expression. This marks the completion of Venus’ arduous, yet ardent, retrograde journey over the last few months, and when Venus squares the lunar nodes on December 29, you will be faced with an important decision that only your heart can make. By this point in the month, the Sun and Mercury will be building toward a clarifying conversation or moment of personal gnosis you’ll have on January 1 involving your partnerships. Your relationship to home, family life, your kids if you have them, and romantic love in general has been undergoing a sea change, and this will bring things together in a way that will start to finally feel more settled in your soul.

Though you’ve got plenty to keep you busy right now, Venus can help you ease into greater enjoyment of where you’re at. This wouldn’t be a bad month to take a real vacation for once, take the kids somewhere fun, go see some live music, and fill your calendar up with date nights (with a lover, with a friend, with yourself, those all count). All work and no play makes you a dull crab, and you need to fill your well back up before you can expect yourself to perform at the level you’re expecting yourself to in 2027.

You’ve been devoting a lot of energy to establishing a version of home that fits who you currently are, and right now, things seem to be coming together on that front. Perhaps you’ve been up to your neck in moving boxes these last few weeks, or maybe you’ve been circling around some deep, existential questions about family and what you want yours to look like. Some of you may have finally pulled the trigger on a risky international move that required you to move literal mountains to get your visa approved, and now you’re being confronted with the reality of how this will change all of your relationships to the people you’re still connected to back home. The research and deliberation phase is now wrapping up, and what remains is to simply go through with your decision, knowing that you are moving through a portal created by that choice.

Amid all the other activity this month, Jupiter’s station retrograde on December 12 comes through the most prominently for you. Since June 30, Jupiter has been moving through Leo, bringing a swell of momentum to your growth and personal trajectory. Maybe the real momentum was just the confidence you gained all along? You may have shared more of your creative talent with the world, or been hard at work birthing something special into the world (this could absolutely include a literal pregnancy, or a desire to have one). Regardless, your labor of love is shifting into a slightly different gear for the next couple months. Jupiter will be retrograde until April, which gives you ample time to try a new approach, to pause and digest what you’ve learned, or to incubate your dream a little longer while you deal with the obstacles in your way and reconsider what you’re truly striving for.

Mid-month, the dual direct stations of Saturn and Neptune in your 9th house of foreign places and education could signal more than “game on” related to a possible long-distance move. If you’ve been hard at work pursuing a degree, your path forward becomes a little more certain around this time as more news comes in related to your eligibility for student loans or doing the independent study you had in mind. You might also find yourself locking in in other respects—recommitting your energy to a long-distance relationship, challenging the various spiritual and intellectual authorities in your midst, continuing a legal battle, or deciding to go through with some ambitious travel plans in spite of the trouble and red tape you’ll encounter along the way. The path less traveled is surely the one worth experiencing, but the catch is that it’s probably up to you to clear the way for yourself.

If the weight of all your backlogged grief and anger is starting to catch up to you, let it. There’s a sense that while you’re now out of the frying pan, you’re moving into the fire. That’s a dramatic-sounding metaphor to convey that you’ve reached that point where the immediate emergency has passed, but now your body feels safe enough to let you know how much it was relying on adrenaline to hold you together. This is not one of those times when you can just “push through it” and expect to keep functioning at your normal baseline. Mars spends all month getting ready to go retrograde in Virgo, which is another way of saying your “little engine that could” is slowing down over the course of December. By the time everyone’s back from the holidays, you will either be significantly tapped out or too irritated to put up with status quo for much longer, so try to plan ahead now to give yourself some extra breathing room and space to pivot during the first three months of 2027. This doesn’t have to be a huge crisis necessarily, but it will ask you to take certain aspects of your existence to the chopping block.

Meanwhile, you’ve got holiday parties to plan and a house to get in order. Much of your immediate concerns involve family, loved ones, and any possible festivities you will lend your thoughtful touches to. Venus spends the month in Scorpio, helping you reestablish connections to friends, siblings, and neighbors after the recent retrograde threw some of those relationships into question. This is probably a good time to take that trip to visit your bestie you’ve been promising for months, but do be mindful of some interpersonal turbulence coming your way in early December. There are some angry, aggravating aspects occurring between December 4 and 9, which seem especially primed to make you bicker with your family or pop off on social media. Some things absolutely need to be said, but your truth bombs will probably cut deeper than they usually do right now, which is saying a lot.

If that whole kerfuffle doesn’t kill the vibe too badly, the full moon in Cancer on December 23 brings the social gathering together. You could be throwing an event or party, going on a big group trip, getting people in on your vision, or giving something back to your community. More broadly, this moment comes with a sense of knowing who your people are (and who they aren’t). Yeah, you probably will be more selective when it comes to friendships going forward, but there’s also some sweetness and renewal and, dare I say, celebration happening in this moment.

It’s time to put your money where your mouth is and raise your standards across every aspect of your life. You’ve been deep in your soul searching these past couple of months, and some of that may have directly involved your finances (in the sense that you’re ready for a higher maximum capacity of “what you can have and comfortably hold,” but you weren’t quite sure how to get there yet). Venus reenters Scorpio on December 4 and spends the rest of the month retracing the territory where it went retrograde earlier, and then, most crucially, moving beyond that point. This December, you are closing the loop on where you got emotionally knotted up previously, and you are resolving your own inner alchemy process by taking some concrete steps towards the vision you’re now holding for your life.

A raise or other kind of professional level-up seems within reach right now, given that there’s a full moon in Cancer on December 23. This is a moment for you to see the extent of the harvest you’ve cultivated in your career this year, and it comes at a time when you’re ready to level up in your earning power and standard of living. Perhaps you’re ready for your annual review, or you’re cooking up new offers and services to launch to your clientele. You are probably feeling particularly fertile right now in the sense that you have more to potentially give to the world, which is, coincidentally, a necessary prerequisite to actually receiving more. Don’t be discouraged if you feel you still have further to go, or if your current progress falls short of what you’re able to imagine for yourself. That’s actually a great place to be. Pay attention to the power of the intentional choices you can make around December 29, when Venus squares the lunar nodes. You are crossing an invisible threshold that will put you on a new path.

By the way, all this talk about “standards” also has to do with relationships of every kind, and you will reach a felt turning point this month with certain connections, friendships, and partnerships. Realistically, this is just the logical next step of realizing you’ve outgrown certain dynamics and that you’re ready for something different. Try to be careful with how you communicate where you’re at, especially between December 6 and 9, because the potential for a foot-in-mouth moment is certainly there. These could also show up as a couple of particularly hectic days to be on the road—which includes your regular commute across town—so try to plan accordingly if you can. It’s always good to know who to call for backup, especially if you’re traveling in a foreign country.

Just remember that if they didn’t love you at your October crashout, they don’t deserve you at your December glow-up. You start the month strong with Mercury in Scorpio squaring the lunar nodes on December 1, which may find you responding to someone with a delayed decision you can finally feel good about making. Then, on December 4, Venus re-enters Scorpio and starts to close the loop on the retrograde journey it went on these past couple of months. Venus will hang out in your rising sign all December, which is not only a sign that you’ll be taking some real, concrete steps to change the things that have been making you unhappy, but also a bit of a personal glamor spell to help you recover your je ne sais quoi. Just like Mercury at the start of the month, Venus is building up to a fateful square to the nodes too, on December 29. This is a turning point that asks you to prove with your actions, and not just your words, that you love yourself first.

Certainly, this doesn’t need to find you in a solitary state — there’s a very good chance that there’s a love or other kind of relationship story at the heart of this process. The turning point in question could invite you to go all in with another person, or to walk away when love is no longer being served at the table. Coupled with a full moon in Cancer (your 9th house of foreign places) on December 23, the forecast calls for a high chance of overseas adventures while you’re going through these subtle transformations. You could take a trip with your beau that helps you both confirm where things are headed, or maybe just have your eyes opened by another culture to ways you could be treating yourself better. For what it’s worth, this does seem like the sort of astrology that would invite you to try a new beauty procedure on your travels, or to experiment with new styles and looks.

Things are also shifting on the work front for you right now, but that could be as subtle as taking on new projects and potentially as major as getting a new role. However, it’s very possible that something about your next step is provisional in nature—you could be filling in for someone’s maternity leave, for example, or reaching the next stepping stone on your path to the ultimate goal destination. You’re still on your way to potentially realizing your dreams or leveling up, but these next few months will challenge you in certain ways, and potentially, they will make you reconsider your strategy too. From now until April, just assume you’re still in the trial-and-error phase of whatever you’re trying to pull off. You will have enough information by Q2 to move forward more intentionally.

It looks like you might need to alienate some people to become the most authentically expressed version of yourself. You’ve been sitting on these feelings for some time, and you’ve even prepared yourself emotionally for what the potential fallout could feel like. It’s not that you’ve reached some sort of enlightened, unbothered place where you no longer feel like any of this has the potential to affect you. It’s more that the pain of being misattuned to has gotten so uncomfortable that you’re willing to have it any other way. You feel pretty clear on who your people are, and finding your way back into an aligned sense of community is part of what’s given you the confidence to break away from your fake friends. This month is when you find your voice again, and this will likely scatter some dominoes into motion.

Your loudest moment of potentially rocking the boat comes at the start of the month, especially between December 4 and 9. Venus reenters your 12th house of isolation and hidden enemies, and a cantankerous Mercury-Mars-Uranus square pops off across the most energetically active houses in your chart, heralded by Mercury entering Sagittarius and making you into the loudmouth you were born to be. Yes, this will probably be messier than it needs to be, and you still need to take some amount of ownership over the way your words land, because under these skies, conversations can go off the rails pretty quickly. But it’s also true that speaking with less inhibition can heal you energetically and open up a world of possibilities that you couldn’t see before. So, do with that information what you will. The new moon in Sagittarius lands inside this chaos on December 8, setting you on a new trajectory that will really bear fruit in June.

In the midst of all this, your ruling planet, Jupiter, goes retrograde on December 12. However, the stillness will be felt all month. The next few months will be your time to pause and rethink what it is you’re doing, as well as to digest all the big, beautiful experiences you’ve had recently. Part of this is probably connected to what you need to get off your chest, because it could be that you’re questioning your own worldview or needing some more introspection around your politics. You could also be getting ready to lay low a bit with travel, especially if you’ve been running yourself ragged these last few months. It’s not entirely unlikely that you’ll be on the move this month, but it does seem as though you’ll need to seriously rethink the way you’ve been going about your adventures. Practice extra caution between the 4th and 9th, because the energy on these days is more volatile and more predisposed to things going wrong. The end of December is generally more favorable for travel.

If you’re feeling called to rest right now, and you can, let yourself. You might be a little burned out from all the visibility and public engagement lately, and from a general sense of having to be “on” for the world. The month begins with the Sun traveling through your 12th house, which generally puts you in the mood to retreat and exist in goblin mode, in a little hermit cave where you don’t have to be seen. Though there’s a certain amount of needing to maintain a presence online or in your community this month, you can probably accomplish this with your camera off and your mic on mute, so to speak. And though a getaway to somewhere warm never hurt anyone, it’s very possible that you’ll feel your will or capability to travel sputtering as we get closer to January (especially if the trip ends up being more trouble than it’s worth). Be forewarned that certain aspects of your 2027 travel plans could be derailed by the upcoming Mars Retrograde, or at best, stress-tested. Maybe don’t lock down anything too firmly just yet.

The big news for you in December is that your ruling planet, Saturn, is stationing direct in your 4th house of home and family (exact on December 10, but felt all month). This could certainly create a gravitational pull that anchors you back to home base or makes you less inclined to go out for the time being. The real deal, however, is that a period of relative flexibility is firming up again to lock you into a new set of circumstances, and this will likely have something to do with your living situation or your parents. The ongoing project of creating more housing stability for yourself or navigating a kind of winter with your family continues, and this time, there’s probably less trial and error involved. You might be getting ready to buy a house or make some other sort of investment to settle down somewhere on a more permanent basis. This could certainly involve decisions related to caring for aging parents or showing up for family in other ways. For some of you, it could look like cutting toxic family members off.

You will feel ready to reemerge again when the Sun enters Capricorn on December 21, and to start taking concrete steps towards your 2027 plans. Some amount of feeling the other shoe drop when it comes to your relationships also hits you in this part of the month, though it is mostly boundary-setting and receiving knowledge of where you stand with certain people in your life that, largely speaking, won’t shock you. ‘Tis the season to embrace where you’re at, and embrace the people who are legitimately in your corner.

Something you’ve been hard at work perfecting is about to get its moment in the sun, or at the very least, its moment at the company all-hands meeting. You are ending the year with a sense of satisfaction that your project is complete, or that a team effort you’ve been a part of is now finally coming together. And while you’re celebrating a job well done and the substantial progress you’ve made, you are also leaning fully into what the next phase of your life will ask of you. There’s a sense that you’re definitively turning the corner in December and preparing to devote yourself to the next level of your mission. Will you accept the call, or has that choice already been made in your heart of hearts?

Look for decisive moments of this nature to show up around December 1 and 29, which is when Mercury and Venus square the lunar nodes from your 10th house of career and public roles. That said, Venus will be transiting this part of the sky all month starting on December 4, closing out the last couple of months of soul-searching and letting you pour your heart and soul into your professional projects. Perhaps it’s time to reveal a bold new rebrand or set of headshots, or maybe you’ll show off something weird and wonderful to the world that will receive plenty of appreciation from your target audience. The people who get it, get it. You were never meant to be everyone’s cup of tea. Side note: This is the sort of influence that could lead to lots of interesting stares when you’re a visitor in someone else’s country. You will likely stand out for one reason or another if you happen to be traveling, and not all of the attention you receive will be comfortable or desirable. However, some of the curiosity will hopefully charm you.

With your ruling planet, Saturn, stationing direct on December 10, you are also more generally exiting a temporary or provisional set of conditions you’ve been in since Julyish. Maybe you’ve enjoyed a little more flexibility during this time, particularly when it comes to how you arrange your schedule and commute. You might need to lock in now to a more fixed routine, which is probably what you need, even if it’s not what you want. This could very well be related to the next big thing you’re about to work on, and the clarity you’re feeling now about the shape it will take. In the meantime, look out for literal or metaphorical roadblocks that show up this month to stall or delay you. Your ability to get around town could be impeded in some way, and you might need to seek an alternate mode of transportation. These issues could find you on your travels, too, so avoid cutting your travel time short if you have somewhere to be.

You’ve got everyone’s attention right now, and you might get even more after you subvert the world’s expectations. There’s a certain degree of controversy that will inevitably follow in your wake this month, but that could simply be the natural result of caring less about the reaction you’re going to get. You’ve spent the last couple of months deeply considering your ethical values and closely held beliefs, and you just so happen to be approaching a moment of feeling freer and less inhibited in how you express yourself. Your words will probably cause the most waves between December 6 and 9, so do with that information what you will. If all attention is good attention in your book, or if you mean to ruffle some feathers, go at it. But if it’s important to you that the things you say are received in the way you intended, this is not the time to drunkenly fire off an insensitive, half-baked thought. You know how people can be, especially on the internet. This game of telephone could handily go off the rails.

This also finds you at a moment of deep internal pause. Your ruling planet, Jupiter, is stationing retrograde (exact on December 12), but effectively, it’s going to feel like things are kind of standing still for you. One of your projects could be hitting a plateau or lull as you get ready to pivot or gather more information, and you might also learn that you need to make some lifestyle adjustments for the sake of your health. You might have to put something on the back burner while more pressing (or exciting) projects demand your immediate attention, and while financial pressure builds to make ends meet.

But in case that sounded like too much mundane energy for one month, it does seem like you’re a good candidate for “rising sign most likely to have a spicy travel romance in December.” Venus will be back in Scorpio, your 9th house of travel and foreign places, and there’s a full moon in Cancer in your 5th house of pleasure and romance on December 23. It’s not all necessarily cute, and it’s not all necessarily fun and games, but if you were looking for a sign to go somewhere new and replenish your soul with a change of scenery, this would be a decent time to do it. Just be mindful that Venus will square Pluto on December 9, and that Mars is also slowing down to go retrograde in your 7th house of relationships in January. No one’s promising that emotional complications won’t follow, but at least you’ll have some new inspiration to feed the muse with.
